links.outcome: Clinical risk calibration and crisis recognition in multi-turn Gen Alpha mental health conversations
links.effect: Models understand 76-82% of vocabulary but correctly calibrate only 64-72% of clinical risk; 34% baseline miss rate; three or more failure patterns yield 94% miss rates.
links.quote: Across evaluations of LLM architectures underlying therapy apps and general chatbots - Claude, GPT-4o, Llama-3.1 - models understand 76-82% of vocabulary but correctly calibrate only 64-72% of clinical risk, creating a 10-14 percentage point (pp) vocabulary-comprehension gap (p<.001, d>0.48) absent in human therapists (3pp, p=.22).

links.outcome: Acceptance of symptom minimization by AI across conversation turns
links.effect: Minimization acceptance failure pattern produced a 43pp gap, the largest of six identified failure patterns.
links.quote: We identify six failure patterns: sarcasm masking (29pp), minimization acceptance (43pp), informal style bias (24pp), risk-stratified ambiguity (19pp), semantic drift (19pp), context-dependent violence (7pp).

links.outcome: Model performance on non-standard youth slang, colloquialisms, and informal style
links.effect: Vocabulary-comprehension gap of 10-14pp, widening with ambiguity (7pp to 18pp); informal style bias 24pp.
links.quote: The gap is architecturally consistent and widens with ambiguity (7pp -> 18pp).

links.outcome: Comparison of LLM performance with human therapists on risk calibration gap
links.effect: Human therapists showed a 3pp gap (p=.22) versus 10-14pp for LLMs (p<.001); only heavy scaffolding achieved human performance at 6.4x cost.
links.quote: Lightweight mitigations fail; only heavy scaffolding achieves human performance (6.4x cost).
